description:
Project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)

Context / why now:
Redwood’s largest Dedicated and high-throughput Hosted workloads increasingly run tensor-parallel (TP) across multiple GPUs per replica. Under sustained load (mixed prefill/decode, long context, bursty concurrency), the runtime has known failure modes that manifest as request hangs, GPU stalls, and downstream timeouts. These issues are costly: they inflate p99 latency, trigger autoscaling thrash, and occasionally escalate into Sev1 incidents for enterprise customers.

Goals:
1) Eliminate known runtime hangs/timeouts in TP execution under load (primary).
2) Improve detection/diagnostics so future TP stalls are caught early with actionable signals (GPU/collective/scheduler visibility).
3) Add regression coverage (repro harness + perf canary) to prevent re-introducing TP deadlocks.
4) Provide safe mitigations: watchdogs, controlled abort/retry paths, and operational runbooks for on-call.

Scope (in-scope areas):
- Runtime scheduler: queue/backpressure interactions, prefill/decode interleaving, multi-stream coordination, and fairness logic that can starve collectives.
- Kernel + comms boundary: NCCL collective ordering, stream synchronization points, event/graph capture constraints, and “silent stall” scenarios.
- Memory/KV cache behavior under TP: fragmentation/compaction interactions that can amplify stalls.
- Observability: metrics, tracing spans, structured logs to identify whether a hang is compute, comms, or scheduler.
- Reliability controls: watchdog timeouts, circuit breakers/load-shedding hooks, controlled replica drain/restart.

Out of scope:
- Model quality/evals (unless used only as workload generators).
- Major architecture rewrite of TP execution; this project focuses on targeted correctness + stability hardening.

Stakeholders / teams:
- Eng Serving Runtime (Kernel + Scheduling): Hiro Tanaka (Mgr Kernels), Sofia Ivanova (Mgr Scheduling), Noah Patel (Sr Staff), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Omar El‑Sayed, Samir Qureshi, Marcus Reed.
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (Dir), Rafael Mendes (Mgr), Tomáš Novák, Aisha Bello.
- Product (reliability/rollouts and Dedicated customer impact): Paula Mendes, Lauren Bishop.
- Customer Success/Support as escalation interface (via Jira/Slack/CS playbooks).

High-level plan / phases (6–8 weeks total):
- Phase 0 (Week 1): Triage + reproduce: pick top 2–3 hang signatures, build deterministic repro in benchmark-lab/perf-canary, and tag incidents/tickets.
- Phase 1 (Weeks 2–4): Instrumentation + targeted fixes: scheduler ordering fixes, NCCL stream/event ordering hardening, watchdog + safe abort, and KV/cache edge-case handling.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Regression tests + canary rollout: perf-canary scenarios, stress suite, staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 6–8): Operationalization: runbooks, dashboard/alerts, postmortem/incident-review, and finalize known-issues/workarounds.

Deliverables:
- A set of runtime PRs implementing fixes and instrumentation.
- Linear initiative + linked subtasks with dependencies and rollout checkpoints.
- Confluence design/ADR(s), known-issues page updates, runbooks, and an incident review/postmortem if tied to a Sev.
- Drive working docs: repro notes, benchmark sheets, rollout checklist, and weekly notes.
- Slack coordination threads and (if applicable) incident channel artifacts.
- Support artifacts (Jira) and customer-facing coordination (Fireflies/Gmail/HubSpot) for affected enterprise accounts.
